question: What were weighted civil filings per judgeship nationally in FY2020?

record.final_text:
Nationally, weighted civil filings per judgeship in FY2020 were **322** (JFF-2025, Table 6.2).

Note this figure was revised: it was first published as **554** (JB-2020, Table X-1A) and stayed at 554 through JFF-2022, then dropped to 322 starting with JFF-2023 and has remained there since. The published tables don't explain the revision. As an unconfirmed inference (not an official statement), the drop is consistent with N.D. Fla.'s directly filed MDL cases (which contributed ~211 of the original 554 points) being excluded or down-weighted in the revised series — but this needs AO confirmation.

revision_notes.text: FY2020 Weighted civil filings per judgeship: 554 (JB-2020 to JFF-2022) → 322 (JFF-2023 to JFF-2025). The tables' notes don't explain the change.

In JB-2020 Table X-1A, N.D. Fla.'s filings contribute 211 points to the national 554; the later edition's figure is 232 points lower. That is consistent with the revised series excluding or down-weighting those cases (mostly directly filed MDL cases), but no published note says so. Unconfirmed: needs AO confirmation.

provenance.series: Judicial Facts and Figures
provenance.definition: Civil filings multiplied by Federal Judicial Center case weights (which reflect the relative judge time each case type needs), divided by authorized judgeships. The Judicial Conference uses weighted filings when assessing judgeship needs.
